character_facts: Honorata attempts to protect her child through deception during interrogation.
Honorata carries an implanted bomb and ultimately remains behind because she cannot safely leave with her loved ones.
Aghnar is Honorata's son and uses prosthetic weapons in combat.
Othon is Aghnar's father and acts to destroy the Cetacyborg.
The Mother Superior leads the Shabda-Oud group pursuing them.
characters_present: two assassins accompanying the Mother Superior
hooded Shabda-Oud witches or priestesses shown in the inset art
five unidentified character portraits shown at the bottom, likely major figures from the recap/cast
continuity_links: This page is an explicit 'previously' recap that sets up the next chapter after Honorata's death and Okhar's destruction.
It establishes the revenge motive carried forward by the surviving father and son.
dialogue_meaning: There is no scene dialogue; the page functions as a narrated recap of prior events.
The recap explains the chain of events leading from the Shabda-Oud's arrival and interrogation of Honorata to Okhar's destruction and the surviving family members' vow of revenge.
lore_facts: The Shabda-Oud have a Mother Superior, witches or priestesses, and assassins.
A Cetacyborg is described as a gigantic semi-organic vessel.
Epyphite-tipped prosthetics are effective enough to help Aghnar overcome the assassins.
The Mother Superior can engage in telepathic combat.
Honorata can link her power to her son's power.
Othon pilots or uses a craft called the Metacraft.
The Metabunker is capable of leaving the planet and observing its destruction from space.
Honorata has an artificial heart, and the implanted micro-H bomb is connected to it.
Okhar is destroyed in a nuclear annihilation.
plot_events: The page recaps that the Mother Superior of the Shabda-Oud arrives on Okhar aboard a giant semi-organic vessel called a Cetacyborg, with two assassins.
Honorata is interrogated and lies that her child is a hermaphrodite, claiming an accident caused the child's amputation.
The witches attempt to examine the child and uncover the deception, but Aghnar attacks them with claw-tipped prostheses.
Aghnar defeats the assassins because his prosthetics are tipped with epyphite, then fights the Mother Superior in a telepathic duel while Honorata links her power to his.
Othon enters his Metacraft to destroy the sleeping Cetacyborg, ultimately destroying it from inside after its outer skin repels missiles.
Honorata reveals that a micro-H bomb was implanted inside her from the beginning and that it is tied to her artificial heart.
Honorata cannot leave with her family because doing so would endanger them, and the surgeons cannot remove the implant.
Father and son depart in the Metabunker and witness Honorata and Okhar being annihilated from space.
